Reviewing Incident Reports

subset_review.Rmd

You can process person-level, class-level, and mixed incident reports. Each row describes one incident affecting one person or one class. A table can contain reports for many people or classes. A class report is reviewed as one incident, even when it affects several people.

Report type level targetId contains Additional input
Person-level "person" The person ID for that row, e.g. "P1" None for an item report
Class-level "class" The class ID for that row, e.g. "K1" persons: the person-to-class mapping
Mixed: people and classes "person" or "class" per row The person or class ID for that row persons: the person-to-class mapping

“Mixed” describes a table containing both kinds of report. Each row still uses level = "person" or level = "class". See workflow 3.

All three input options have the same steps: describe the incident, check the selected responses, then review and decide whether to recode them. prepareSubsetInfo() selects responses; visualSubsetRecode() opens the review.

Every issue table needs the same five columns: issueId, level, targetId, scope, and target. Each issueId must be unique. The examples also include the optional comment column; use "" when no comment is needed. head() shows the input table in each example.

Shared example data

Three people answered two items. Use merged response data, before aggregating subunits into items. In these examples, "mci" is the replacement code for responses invalidated by an incident.

review_data <- data.frame(
  ID = c("P1", "P2", "P3"),
  I1 = c(1, 0, 1),
  I2 = c(0, 1, 0)
)
review_data
#>   ID I1 I2
#> 1 P1  1  0
#> 2 P2  0  1
#> 3 P3  1  0

Workflow 1: person-level reports

Example: display errors affected item I2 for P1 and P3. Enter both reports in one table, with a separate issueId for each. Set level = "person" and put the affected person’s ID in targetId on each row.

person_issues <- data.frame(
  issueId = c("V1", "V2"), level = "person", targetId = c("P1", "P3"),
  scope = "item", target = "I2", comment = c("Display error", "")
)
head(person_issues)
#>   issueId  level targetId scope target       comment
#> 1      V1 person       P1  item     I2 Display error
#> 2      V2 person       P3  item     I2

Resolve the affected responses:

person_info <- prepareSubsetInfo(review_data, person_issues)
person_info[c("issueId", "ID", "datCols")]
#>   issueId ID datCols
#> 1      V1 P1      I2
#> 2      V2 P3      I2

The selection contains P1/I2 and P3/I2, reviewed as two separate incidents. No class or booklet tables are needed. Start the review in an interactive R session:

person_result <- visualSubsetRecode(review_data, person_info, toRecodeVal = "mci")

Choose yes, all values for each report, then yes to end the review. The result is:

person_result$dat
#>   ID I1  I2
#> 1 P1  1 mci
#> 2 P2  0   1
#> 3 P3  1 mci

P1’s and P3’s responses to I2 change. P2’s responses and all responses to I1 keep their original values.

Workflow 2: class-level reports

Example: a display error affected item I2 for everyone in class K1. Set level = "class" and put the class ID in targetId. Supply persons so the function knows who belongs to that class:

persons <- data.frame(
  ID = c("P1", "P2", "P3"), classId = c("K1", "K1", "K2")
)
class_issue <- data.frame(
  issueId = "V3", level = "class", targetId = "K1",
  scope = "item", target = "I2", comment = ""
)
head(class_issue)
#>   issueId level targetId scope target comment
#> 1      V3 class       K1  item     I2

Resolve the affected responses:

class_info <- prepareSubsetInfo(review_data, class_issue, persons = persons)
class_info[c("issueId", "ID", "datCols")]
#>   issueId ID datCols
#> 1      V3 P1      I2
#> 2      V3 P2      I2

The single class report selects P1/I2 and P2/I2. Both rows retain issueId = "V3", so you review them together and make one decision for the class report. P3 belongs to K2 and is outside the selection.

class_result <- visualSubsetRecode(review_data, class_info, toRecodeVal = "mci")

Choose yes, all values, then yes to end the review:

class_result$dat
#>   ID I1  I2
#> 1 P1  1 mci
#> 2 P2  0 mci
#> 3 P3  1   0

The difference from workflow 1 is the affected people: the same item is recoded for everyone in K1, while P3’s responses stay unchanged. Class IDs must identify classes uniquely across the data set, including across schools.

Workflow 3: mixed reports

Example: process the two person reports and the class report together. Combine them in one table. Each row keeps its own level, targetId, and unique issueId:

issues <- rbind(person_issues, class_issue)
head(issues)
#>   issueId  level targetId scope target       comment
#> 1      V1 person       P1  item     I2 Display error
#> 2      V2 person       P3  item     I2              
#> 3      V3  class       K1  item     I2

Supply the class membership table persons, as in workflow 2:

subset_info <- prepareSubsetInfo(review_data, issues, persons = persons)
summary(subset_info)
#>   issueId  level targetId persons items cells overlappingCells
#> 1      V1 person       P1       1     1     1                1
#> 2      V2 person       P3       1     1     1                0
#> 3      V3  class       K1       2     1     2                1

Start one review for the whole table:

mixed_result <- visualSubsetRecode(review_data, subset_info, toRecodeVal = "mci")

The review presents V1 (P1), V2 (P3), and V3 (class K1) separately. Choose yes, all values for each report, then yes to end the review:

mixed_result$dat
#>   ID I1  I2
#> 1 P1  1 mci
#> 2 P2  0 mci
#> 3 P3  1 mci

All three people’s responses to I2 are recoded. P1/I2 occurs in both V1 and V3; resetting one report keeps a recoding still required by the other. Choose reset to original values to withdraw a previous recoding; no leaves it unchanged. All three workflows preserve existing NA responses.

If the incident affects a block

In all three workflows, level answers who is affected? and scope answers which responses are affected? An item report uses scope = "item". For an entire block, also supply booklets, blocks, and rotation.

For example, P1 and P2 are both in K1 but use different block orders:

booklets <- data.frame(
  booklet = c("X", "Y"), block1 = c("A", "B"), block2 = c("B", "A")
)
blocks <- data.frame(
  subunit = c("I1", "I2"), block = c("A", "B"), subunitBlockPosition = 1
)
rotation <- data.frame(ID = c("P1", "P2", "P3"), booklet = c("X", "Y", "X"))

To report a problem with the first block in class K1, keep the class target and change the scope to "blockPosition":

block_issue <- class_issue
block_issue$scope <- "blockPosition"
block_issue$target <- "1"
head(block_issue)
#>   issueId level targetId         scope target comment
#> 1      V3 class       K1 blockPosition      1
block_info <- prepareSubsetInfo(
  review_data, block_issue, persons = persons,
  booklets = booklets, blocks = blocks, rotation = rotation
)
block_info[c("ID", "datCols", "block", "blockPosition")]
#>   ID datCols block blockPosition
#> 1 P1      I1     A             1
#> 2 P2      I2     B             1

This selects P1/I1 and P2/I2: the first block is A for P1 and B for P2. Review block_info just like class_info above. To select named block A instead, use scope = "block", target = "A"; that selects I1 for both people.

Pause and continue

For a longer review, choose a new checkpoint filename when starting:

result <- visualSubsetRecode(
  review_data, subset_info, toRecodeVal = "mci", checkpoint = "review.rds"
)
# Choose "pause review (resume later)". In a later R session:
library(eatPrep)
result <- visualSubsetRecode(state = "review.rds")

Completed decisions are saved automatically. Resume with state to keep the original values and earlier decisions. Continue your data preparation with result$dat; result$subsetInfo contains the decision history.

For project data, the design tables can come from inputList. After recodeData(), also pass subunits = inputList$subunits to map original item names to recoded columns. See ?prepareSubsetInfo and ?visualSubsetRecode for input requirements, review options, and checkpoint recovery.
